official_measurement_examples.name: Statutory determination periods
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current guidance states statutory limits of 13 weeks for major development, 10 weeks for technical-details consent and specified public-service infrastructure, 8 weeks for other development, and 16 weeks where an application is subject to EIA.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning guarantee distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: The planning guarantee is government policy and does not replace statutory time limits; it uses 26 weeks for major and 16 weeks for non-major decisions before appeal time is considered.

official_measurement_examples.name: PPA process not outcome
official_measurement_examples.fact: A Planning Performance Agreement commits parties to a process and timetable and does not commit the local planning authority to a particular decision outcome.

official_measurement_examples.name: Extension-of-time context
official_measurement_examples.fact: A written extension of time changes the agreed determination period but is not the same thing as the original statutory deadline and does not imply permission will be granted.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 performance statistics
official_measurement_examples.fact: For January to March 2026, 91% of major applications were decided within 13 weeks or agreed time while only 19% were decided within the statutory 13 weeks; the two measures must not be conflated.

official_measurement_examples.name: Performance-agreement prevalence
official_measurement_examples.fact: In January to March 2026, 43% of all planning decisions involved a recorded performance agreement and 77% of major decisions did so; this is a process statistic, not a permission-success rate.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 designation notices
official_measurement_examples.fact: MHCLG published current designation and de-designation notices on 15 June 2026; designation status is authority/category/effective-date specific and must not be inferred from an old performance table.

official_measurement_examples.name: Designation scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Designation can apply separately to major and non-major applications and enables specified applications to be submitted directly to the Planning Inspectorate; it does not transfer every planning function or determine parcel permission.

core_rules: agreed extension is not original statutory deadline
planning guarantee is not statutory time limit
in-time statistic including agreements is not statutory-only statistic
performance-agreement rate is not approval rate
designation must retain category and effective date
designation does not transfer all applications automatically
non-determination appeal right requires applicable deadline context
performance metrics do not establish parcel ownership
performance metrics do not establish infrastructure capacity
authority designation does not calculate development yield
policy proposal is not operative fee rule until implemented
no parcel performance clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, Planning Inspectorate, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked on 2026-07-26. April-July 2026 determination guidance, statistics and designation notices retained with statutory/agreed-time/PPA/designation distinctions; no parcel promotion.
